absent: eventfd counter drain semantics distinguishing semaphore versus counter mode
eventfd poll readiness rules, release path and identifier lifecycle
epoll control add, modify, delete validation and cycle-check outcome
epoll wait collection, timeout and signal-interaction semantics
overflow-chain insertion path from poll callbacks and ready-list promotion rules

findings.text: A helper obtains a file reference from a numeric descriptor and confirms membership in the eventfd family by comparing operations tables. Unknown descriptors yield a bad-descriptor failure and other file kinds yield an invalid-argument failure with the reference dropped.

Two system entries create a counter notification object: one takes only an initial value, the other also takes creation flags. Both delegate to a shared creator that validates flags and returns a new descriptor or a negative error.

Read requires room for an eight byte unsigned value. An empty counter with nonblocking or nowait posture fails without sleeping, otherwise the caller sleeps interruptibly until nonzero and may be restarted by signals. Success drains through a helper, notifies writability waiters, marks task context around wakeup, and delivers exactly eight bytes; short delivery reports a fault.

Write demands exactly eight bytes from user space and rejects the all-ones input. Overflow means insufficient headroom below the unsigned maximum. Without headroom, nonblocking posture fails immediately while blocking posture sleeps interruptibly until headroom appears. Success adds to the counter, notifies readability waiters with task-context marking, and reports eight.
Descriptor-info display samples the counter under protection and reports the value in hexadecimal, a numeric identifier, and whether semaphore mode is enabled.
Eventfd file behaviour binds release, poll, iterated read, plain write and a no-op seek, plus a descriptor-info hook when process reporting is enabled.

Creation enforces compile-time equivalence of eventfd flag constants with standard file flags and a fixed semaphore bit, rejects unknown flag bits, allocates and initializes reference count, wait queue, counter and flags, requests an anonymous read-write file with nowait support, allocates a numeric identifier and publishes the descriptor.

Private mask groups EPOLLWAKEUP, EPOLLONESHOT, EPOLLET and EPOLLEXCLUSIVE. Readiness grouping combines EPOLLIN and EPOLLOUT. Exclusive-compatible set allows EPOLLIN, EPOLLOUT, EPOLLERR, EPOLLHUP, EPOLLWAKEUP, EPOLLET and EPOLLEXCLUSIVE.

Nesting limit is four. Maximum reportable events equals the largest signed integer divided by one user event record size. Inactive overflow marker is an all-bits-set pointer value. Per-item cost covers one interest item plus one poll attachment. Reverse-path tally depth is five.

Poll attachment holds a singly linked successor, a back reference to its owning interest item, an embedded wait element for insertion into a target queue, and a cached pointer to the queue head it is attached to.

Interest item overlays tree linkage and deferred-free linkage in a union, carries ready-list linkage, an overflow successor using the inactive marker when unlinked, a key identifying file and descriptor, a head of poll attachments, a back pointer to the owning context, file-list linkage, an RCU-protected wakeup source, and the user interest record.

Poll context holds a lifetime and control mutex, two wait queues for waiter sleep and poll notification, a ready list with protecting spinlock and sequence counter, a cached tree root, a singly linked overflow chain, wakeup source, creator accounting, backing file, generation and reference state for cycle checks, reference count and deferred-free linkage, plus optional busy-poll tuning and nesting tracking.

Control context records the poll instance being inserted into, a sentinel-terminated list of visited file groups, and a fixed-size per-depth tally. File-group header holds an interest hash list, a list successor and a file pointer. A poll-table wrapper pairs a poll table with its interest item.

Eventfd counter and its wait queue are guarded by the queue lock with interrupts disabled across check, sleep, update and wakeup. Diagnostic sampling takes the same lock briefly. File private data supplies the protected state.

Ready and overflow state is guarded by a spinlock with interrupts disabled plus a sequence counter around transitions. A mutex serializes collection, cleanup, exit and control paths. The wakeup-source pointer is read under that mutex or under RCU. A global nested mutex and generation counter support cycle checks. Poll-wait wakeups use a nested interrupt-saving lock keyed by chain depth in one build and a plain wakeup in the other.

Overflow chain has three postures: inactive marker when idle, null while a scan owns the ready list, and a LIFO chain of newly ready items during the scan. Entering a scan moves the ready list to a private batch and arms collection. Exiting drains the chain, re-queues items not already linked while holding their wakeup sources, restores inactive posture under sequence protection, returns leftover batch items, relaxes the poll wakeup source, and wakes waiters if ready items remain.

Interest ordering compares file identity first then descriptor number. Ready linkage is tested by emptiness of the ready link. Scanning posture is tested by comparing the overflow head against the inactive marker with single-copy reads. Availability is true when the ready list is non-empty, when scanning is active, or when the sequence counter moved during the check. Poll-file identity is by operations-table equality.

Busy timeout compares current time against start plus configured microseconds when set and otherwise defers to a global helper. Busy mode is active when per-instance microseconds, prefer flag or global mode is set. The NAPI loop runs only with a valid identifier and active mode, reports availability on success, otherwise clears the identifier and optionally resumes interrupts. Identifier capture from socket state occurs only in busy mode and ignores invalid or unchanged values.

Busy-poll tuning exposes set and get commands. Set copies parameters from user space, requires zero pad, bounds microseconds to the signed maximum, restricts the prefer flag to zero or one, requires privilege for budget above NAPI weight, then publishes the three values. Get returns the stored triple. Unknown commands report unrecognized ioctl; builds without busy support report unsupported operation. Suspend and resume of NAPI interrupts apply only with a valid identifier and prefer mode.

Queue detachment uses RCU and an acquire load so a null head means teardown is complete and must not be touched, while a non-null head stays alive for removal under the queue lock. Unregistration walks and frees the whole attachment chain. Wakeup-source helpers hold the source awake when present, with mutex-checked, presence-test and RCU variants. Overflow reinsertion preserves FIFO order by head insertion during LIFO drain.

A writable control exposes the per-user watch limit as a bounded long between zero and the largest long, registered under the epoll filesystem namespace at init; builds without that facility compile the init hook to a no-op.

Visited-file tracking treats a null successor as not listed and uses a distinct non-null sentinel to terminate the visited list. Listing takes a file reference, records the file and pushes the header. Unlisting inspects the interest hash under the file lock, clears linkage, frees only when no interests remain, and drops the reference.

Three slab caches hold interest items, poll attachments and file-group headers with post-init read-only protection. A global mutex guards nested poll operations and a monotonic generation supports loop detection.
Poll file identity is determined by operations-table equality. A get operation increments the context reference count to extend lifetime.
